chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abi al-Sabbah, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about the takbir in the two Eids,

So he said: They are twelve: seven in the first [rak'ah] and five in the last. And when you stand in the salat, then say one takbir, and say: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger—up to the end of the report.

key_terms.أَشْهَدُ: I bear witness; the testimony being recited
key_terms.اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ: the total number of takbirs mentioned in the prayer
key_terms.التَّكْبِيرِ: the pronouncement of 'Allahu Akbar' in the Eid prayer
key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: the final or second rak'ah of the prayer
key_terms.الْأُولَى: the first rak'ah of the prayer
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: the two Eid festivals, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha

ai.seo_question: How many takbirs are there in the Eid prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the number of takbirs in salat al-'idayn, stating that they are twelve in total: seven in the first rak'ah and five in the second. It also mentions the opening takbir upon standing in prayer and part of the testimony recited therein, indicating the legal form of this act of worship.
